# Perplexity's Teammates Are AI Agents for Ongoing Work: What It Means

> **In short:** Perplexity has announced Teammates, which it describes as AI agents for complex, ongoing work. Instead of answering one question at a time, they are meant to keep track of a larger job over days or weeks. The announcement does not yet give details on how they work or who can use them.

Most of us have a project that never really ends: a home renovation, a school term paper, a client account that needs attention every week. Each time you return to it, you have to remember where you left off. Perplexity's new Teammates idea is aimed at exactly that kind of problem.

## What an "agent" is

Before we go further, it helps to know the word **agent**. An AI agent is an AI that does more than write a reply. It can work through a series of steps toward a goal, the way a helper would take a task off your plate. Think of the difference between asking a friend for one restaurant suggestion and handing them the whole job of planning a family dinner for the week.

A chatbot usually waits for your next message. An agent is designed to keep going on a task you set up.

## What Perplexity is saying

According to Perplexity's announcement, Teammates are agents built for **complex, ongoing work**. Two parts of that phrase matter:

- **Complex** means the job has several moving pieces, not just one question.
- **Ongoing** means the work does not finish in a single sitting. It stretches over time, and the agent is meant to stay involved.

That is the company's own description of its product. The announcement we are working from is short, so it does not explain the specific features, how you start one, or what it costs. We will not guess at those details. For current information, read Perplexity's official announcement and any product pages it links to.

## Why "ongoing" is the interesting part

Single questions are easy to handle. The harder part of many jobs is the continuity: remembering the goal, the earlier decisions, and what still needs doing. An assistant that can carry that thread forward could save you from re-explaining the same background every time you return to a task.

Here are a few kinds of ongoing work where that idea could matter, in general terms:

- A research project you revisit over several weeks
- A recurring report that needs the same structure each time
- A school assignment broken into stages with deadlines

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you often juggle a long personal project, watch for how Teammates are described in practice. A tool built for ongoing work may suit a multi-week plan better than a one-off chat.
- **For your business or work**: If your job involves projects that run across days or weeks, the "ongoing" focus is the part to watch. Ask whether any new tool you consider can pick up where it left off.
- **If you're just getting started**: You can practice the habit now with any AI chatbot. Write down a multi-step goal, the steps you have finished, and what comes next. That summary is exactly the kind of context an ongoing-work agent would need.

## Wrap-up

Perplexity describes Teammates as AI agents for complex, ongoing work, which is a useful reminder that AI is moving from single answers toward help with longer jobs. The announcement does not yet give the details you would need to start using them, so the sensible move is to read the official announcement directly. Today, pick one project that spans several days and write a short summary of where it stands and what comes next. That summary will help you with any AI tool you choose, now or later.
